summary: Salomon Lefmann was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Münster, Berlin (Ph.D. under Franz Bopp), Heidelberg, and Paris. From 1866, he held various professorial posts at Heidelberg University, becoming an ordinary honorary professor in 1908.

Salomon Munk was a scholar of philosophy, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Berlin, Bonn (under Freytag, Schlegel, and Lassen), and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy, Quatremère, and Chézy. He worked at the Bibliothèque nationale de France and the Collège de France.

Salvador Bucca worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at the University of Pisa and Scuola Normale Superiore. He taught at the National University of Tucumán and National University of Cuyo, and served as Professor of Linguistics at the University of Buenos Aires (1955–1983).

Sam van Schaik is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD from the University of Manchester and studied under Lama Jampa Thaye, Karma Thinley Rinpoche, and Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga. He has held posts at SOAS and the British Library.

Samani Pratibha Pragya is a scholar of religious studies, Indology, and philosophy. She earned her PhD (2011–2017) and later served as a research assistant (attested 2020) at SOAS University of London.

Sambhavi Ganesh works in Indology. She studied at Lady Shri Ram College, Tata Institute of Social Sciences, and the University of Edinburgh (PhD under Radhika Govinda). She worked for Kudumbashree NRO and served as a teaching assistant at King's College London.

Samiran Chandra Chakrabarti is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He held a post at the University of Calcutta and served as Professor (Special Invitee) at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Sampadananda Mishra is a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Pondicherry University. He was appointed Director at Rishihood University in 2021 and Professor at the Hindu University of America in 2022.
Sampan Chakrabarty works in Indology and studied under doctoral supervisor Pallab Sengupta. Chakrabarty held a post as a Research Scholar/Fellow at The Asiatic Society (attested 2026).

Samten Gyaltsen Karmay specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. Educated at Drepung Monastery, SOAS, and the University of London under David Snellgrove, he held posts at SOAS, Collège de France, Paris Nanterre, IIAS, and CNRS, and was President of IATS (1995–2000).

Samuel Beal was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Trinity College, Cambridge, and Durham University. He served as Headmaster of Bramham College, worked for the India Office Records, and was Professor of Chinese at University College London.

Samuel Charles Hill was a historian and Indologist educated at University College School and University College London. He served in the Bengal Educational Service, was a professor at Dhaka College, and was in charge at the National Archives of India and Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Samuel Charters Macpherson was a scholar in the fields of history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at the University of Edinburgh (1822–1823) and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1823).

Samuel De Coster Atkins was an Indologist and linguist who completed his A.B. and Ph.D. at Princeton University. After working as an assistant at Baylor University (1935–1937), he served as Assistant Professor of Classics and Sanskrit at Princeton (1937–1978).

Samuel George Frederick Brandon was a scholar of religious studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at the University of Leeds (~1930–1936) and held a post at the University of Manchester from approximately 1951 to 1971.

Samuel Gottlieb Rudolf Henzi was a religious studies scholar who studied at Bern, Tübingen, Göttingen, and in Paris under Silvestre de Sacy and Chézy. In 1820, he became Professor of Exegesis and Oriental Languages at the University of Tartu.

Samuel Grant Oliphant was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Princeton and Johns Hopkins (under Maurice Bloomfield). He taught at Parsons College, Phillips Exeter, Johns Hopkins, Washington & Jefferson, Olivet, and became Professor of Greek at Grove City College in 1911.
Samuel Heinrich Ribbach was a scholar of Tibetology. He served as a missionary for the Moravian Church from 1892 to 1927 and held a post at the Museum am Rothenbaum.
Samuel Henry Butcher was educated at Marlborough College and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at the University of Edinburgh (~1882–1903) and Harvard University (~1904).

Samuel Henry Kellogg was a scholar of Indology and linguistics educated at Princeton University and Princeton Theological Seminary. He served as an instructor at Allahabad Theological Training School (1873–1876) and Professor of Systematic Theology at Pittsburgh Theological Seminary (1877–1885).
